THE BIRTH OF NOAH — COMPLETE TEXT

FRAGMENT 1 — NOACH'S APPEARANCE AND LAMEKH'S FEAR — 4Q534 Fragment 1

1 [And when the child was born] his body was white as snow and his face shone like the sun and his eyes were like lamps of fire. When he opened his eyes the whole house was illuminated. And his father Lamekh was afraid.

2 And Lamekh went to his father Metushelah and said: I have fathered a strange child. He does not resemble me nor any of the children of men. His appearance is like the appearance of the holy ones of heaven.

3 And Metushelah went to Chanokh his father who was at the ends of the earth among the holy ones, and he told him concerning the child. And Chanokh answered and said: Do not be afraid, Lamekh. The child is yours.

4 For this child has been chosen by YHWH from among all the children of men. He will be righteous in a generation of wickedness and he will be pure in a time of corruption. YHWH will preserve the earth through him.

5 And Chanokh said: Name him Noach. For he will cause rest for the earth and will be a comfort to those who survive the coming judgment. The corruption of the earth has come before YHWH and He has determined to cleanse it.

6 And Metushelah returned to Lamekh and told him all that Chanokh had said. And Lamekh was comforted and he named the child Noach as Chanokh had commanded. And Noach grew and YHWH was with him.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q534 Fragment 1 is the primary witness to the Birth of Noah narrative. The description of Noach's appearance — white as snow, face shining like the sun, eyes like lamps of fire — uses the visual language of divine appointment common in the Afro-Asiatic tradition. This is not a supernatural birth but a child marked from birth for divine purpose.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez Chanokh 106-107 contains a parallel to this narrative. In the Ge'ez version Chanokh also reassures Lamekh that the extraordinary child is his and that YHWH has chosen him for a specific purpose. The Qumran Aramaic text and the Ge'ez version represent parallel witnesses to an ancient Noach-birth tradition that preceded both.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Bereshit contains no account of Noach's birth or his extraordinary appearance. The genealogical notice in Bereshit 5:28-32 simply records that Lamekh fathered Noach and named him as a comfort. The Birth of Noah text preserves the fuller tradition behind that brief genealogical note.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The appearance of extraordinary physical characteristics at birth as a marker of divine election is an ancient Afro-Asiatic literary convention. It does not indicate supernatural parentage — Chanokh explicitly reassures Lamekh that the child is his. It indicates YHWH's advance marking of one He has chosen. Western scholarship, operating within a Christian theological framework, has repeatedly misread this convention as implying miraculous or supernatural birth, projecting later theological categories onto an ancient literary device.
